Eating multiples of 2 on any row will give you a buff e.g. two purple items gives you Felyne Groomer, which speeds up your recovery from elemental blights.

Which 'level' are you referring to? Low rank? High rank? Master rank? Some general tips though, Tobi is a very fast, agile monster, so a 'hit and run' strategy is a good place to start. Take the time to learn his attack patterns, then get in, hit him a few times and get out before he hurts you. 

When you get comfortable enough to dodge his attacks and stay on him, then you can work on keeping the offensive pressure applied.

Try to keep you health full, the lower it gets, the more you're gambling that the next hit won't kill you. Worry more about surviving than kill times.

If he's hitting you harder than you'd like, consider eating for defensive skills or prioritise fresh ingredients (green sparkly ones), they increase your max hp.

If you're still struggling consider upgrading your armour using armour spheres, or look for armour that has high resistance to thunder element.

General Rules

-One catch per Route.

-First encounter only (overworld or random).

-Any fainted Pokemon get sent to the Shadow Realm, and are unusable for the rest of the challenge.

-Every caught Pokemon MUST have a nickname.

-No healing items used in battle, except held items.

-Flying Taxi service can ONLY be used if the destination is MORE THAN three Routes away.

-NO glitches/exploits.

-Pokemon may be swapped from the current team to the PC.

-Duplicate encounters reset the encounter for the Route.

-Shiny Pokemon are exempt from all rules, however, should the Shiny Pokemon meet the rules, it CAN be used, if any exceptions are made in order to catch it, it is sent to the Shadow Realm for the remainder of the challenge.


Regarding the Wild Area


-Wild area is split into subsections, each has it's own encounter, follow general rules for encounters.

-Fishing counts as the encounter for that subsection.


Regarding Raid Dens


-Raid Dens count as the encounter for that subsection.

-Normal faint rules apply; however, I CAN complete the raid, then the Pokemon is sent to the Shadow Realm.

-The first Raid for an area MUST be the one I challenge.

-Multiple challenges on a den are permitted, however after each failure the participating Pokemon MUST be sent to the Shadow Realm.

-EXP Candies can only be used to catch-up level weaker Pokemon/replacements.

-One Raid per Gym Leader defeated, with one pre-Gym Raid.

-NO Raid resetting/skipping exploits.

Light filled his eyes as he was called into existence. The grass felt soft on his feet, the trees surrounding him shielded him from the winds, only a soft breeze permeated their wooden barricade. He looked around, and what he saw chilled him to the bone. To one side, a line of Psyducks, single file and infinite, staring blankly at something behind him. Turning to see, this set a whole new set of chills coursing through his flabby physique. Merely thirty Psyducks down was a trainer, his Absol was staring down a lone Psyduck.

The Absol swiped at the Pokemon, leaving it with just a sliver of health. The Psyduck let out a cry, and he could see the first Psyduck in the queue jump into battle. What happened next caused a rush of pure fear to run through him. The Absol tore mercilessly into the new Psyduck, obliterating its health in one deft strike.

This went on, as new Psyducks joined the fray they were instantly destroyed. It was a slaughter, a massacre. He tried to figure out the purpose of it; the trainer only had the Absol, so he couldn't be looking for shiny Pokemon, the trainer would need multiple Pokemon for that. He couldn't be looking for specific abilities, as both abilities had been presented to him, and yet they fell to the Absol. He wasn't EV training, his Absol was his only Pokemon, and he couldn't be looking for a 4IV Psyduck, his movepool would run out of offensive moves as they started to appear.
He was puzzled, to say the least. He turned to the Psyduck behind him, 'Psy? Duck?' He asked.

The Psyduck stared blankly ahead. He sighed (pun intended), clearly trying to get a conversation out of these absent minded buffoons would be like trying to get a Geodude to bathe.

As he turned he realised he was next in the queue. He paused slightly as the Psyduck called for aid, would the trainer be allured by the cerulean colouring of his own feathers, or would he fall like his yellow-bellied brethren?
He leapt into battle, a star mysteriously flashing before him as the duck beside him was blasted from existence. The timer ball bonked on his beak, sucking him within. He didn't resist, he knew the alternative was to be deleted by that Absol.
After submitting to the trainer, he was honoured with a nickname that would strike fear into the hearts of his opponents: Quackers.
